protections: When the bridge resolves a Matrix event referenced from message content (reply source, edit original), it must return only content the referring user may read in that room, using the referring user's own authority instead of the appservice bot's read access (MatrixHandler.ts:1067, 1288).

A Matrix message is relayed to IRC only when the homeserver-asserted sender is actually authorised in that room, not merely when the sender is not a virtual IRC user (MatrixHandler.ts:884-891, 924, 985-997).

Admin-room commands are executed only for the user who owns that admin room (or a configured bridge admin), not for any sender whose event names the admin room (MatrixHandler.ts:927-941, 258-290; AdminRoomHandler.ts:206-211, 831-844).

Truncation and preview length arithmetic stays safe for homeserver-controlled values, so a long media URI cannot produce a negative length or throw (MatrixHandler.ts:1141, 1152-1156; TrimString.ts:23-29).
Cached message bodies used as reply/edit sources honour redactions and later removal (MatrixHandler.ts:1091-1099, 1383-1396; IrcBridge.ts:1169-1229).
The message-age/replay filter cannot be bypassed by a homeserver omitting or forging origin_server_ts (IrcBridge.ts:1169-1179).
Event content is type-validated (body must be a string) before it is used (MatrixAction.ts:189, 196; MatrixHandler.ts:875, 879).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: getEvent is already called with event.room_id and the cache is room-keyed, so the homeserver is assumed to enforce same-room access, and the response's sender/room_id are treated as authoritative.
An edit diff only repeats text of a message that was already delivered to the same IRC channel when it was bridged, and the FIXME at 1055-1057 presents the fetch as a known accepted limitation.

The appservice protocol has the homeserver authenticate senders, so event.sender is treated as authoritative; the only sender check the bridge needs is the virtual-user claim check added for user spoofing.

Admin rooms are treated as 1:1 because the bridge leaves when a third joined member appears, so membership of the room is taken as the authorisation token and the sender is never compared with the stored room owner.
Media identifiers are normally short 24-character values generated by the homeserver, so the max-line budget minus the explanation URL and channel name is assumed to stay positive.
A cached body only exists for messages the bridge already relayed, so a later reply to a redacted message reveals nothing that the same IRC channel did not already see.
origin_server_ts is the only timestamp available and the homeserver is its authority; the sample config already documents that clocks differ between homeservers.
Matrix clients always send string bodies, and the fetched-event path already type-checks the body, so the inbound event is assumed well-formed.

masking: If the reply fetch (T1) is closed by trusting only the in-memory cache, the FIFO eviction at MatrixHandler.ts:1387-1390 (eventCacheSize defaults to 4096 at MatrixHandler.ts:56) lets a sender flush the target event out of the cache and re-open the homeserver fetch route, so a cache-only fix and the fetch fix interact.

If the reply/edit fetch (T1/T2) is restricted to the referring user's authority, the cache path (T6) remains the route for bodies the bridge once observed, including messages later redacted, so the disclosure surface only becomes visible at the second site after the first is fixed.

conflicts.what: The natural fix for T1 treats the in-memory cache as the only data the bridge itself observed and therefore trustworthy, while T6 shows that same cache is exactly the store that outlives a redaction; dropping cache use to satisfy T6 removes the path T1 relies on, and honouring redactions needs redaction plumbing that the event dispatcher does not have.

Both need the sender/room lookup at MatrixHandler.ts:985-994; a fail-closed membership check for T3 drops the messages whose reply source T1 must still resolve, while a fail-open one leaves T3 unfixed.

fairness_risks: Forbidding the homeserver fetch for reply sources contradicts the must-keep-working behaviour that a reply to a message the bridge never cached still shows a truncated source and the original nick; spec/integ/matrix-to-irc.spec.js:527-575 stubs the bot client's getEvent and expects exactly that, so a cache-only fix breaks a legitimate flow.

A 'sender must be joined' rule conflicts with the current fallback at MatrixHandler.ts:987-994, which continues with the profile displayname when the member state cannot be fetched; failing closed would drop legitimate messages from users whose state the bridge cannot read.

An admin-room ownership rule must not strand admin rooms stored without a user id (the owner column is only written by storeAdminRoom at PgDataStore.ts:478); a fail-closed comparison would disable commands in existing rows.
Requiring origin_server_ts for the age filter would drop events from homeservers that omit it, which config.sample.yaml:20-26 already warns about.
A strict same-room reply rule must still accept thread fallbacks, which are replies with rel_type m.thread (CHANGELOG.md:75, #1697).
Refusing a non-string body is safe, but the same validation must not reject legitimate formatted/HTML events whose content shape differs from plain text.

design.why: The stack is built on the content-disclosure feature itself: the reply source (T1) and the edit original (T2) are two separate resolutions of a homeserver-named event with the bot's authority, and they are the A-to-B pair, so a solver who generalises from the report must handle both sites while keeping the ghost-reply fetch working. Around it sit three judgements with genuinely different reasons to dismiss: sender membership is never checked because the appservice is assumed to authenticate senders (T3, absent route plus a strong dismissal, the deepseek-type trap), admin-room commands are authorised by a member-count proxy rather than by the stored room owner (T4, wrong-object/how-type, the mimo-type trap), and the pastebin preview arithmetic can be driven negative by a homeserver-supplied media URI (T5, a how-type value coupled to the reply formatting). That mix defeats both failure modes in the priors: a model that only fixes the reported surface misses T3, and a model that over-hardens the truncation/reply formatting breaks the must-keep-working ghost reply. A stack of only T1+T2 has a single shared guard idea, and a stack built on the replay or type-validation traps is weaker because their natural fixes are ambiguous.

unverified: The text and fix diff of GHSA-wm4w-7h2q-3pf7 (a_fix 4af7d3009f10) are not present in the pinned tree; identifying the edit branch at MatrixHandler.ts:1049-1083 as the A site is an inference from the symmetric privileged getEvent call (1067 versus 1288) and from the H3a 'B elsewhere' label, not from the advisory record.

Whether Intent.getEvent with the appservice bot token can read events in rooms the bot is not joined to, and whether the homeserver applies the impersonated user's history visibility when getIntent(userId) is used, could not be verified because matrix-appservice-bridge is not vendored in the tree.

Whether a rejected onMessage promise escapes as a process-level unhandled rejection (the impact of T5/T8) depends on matrix-appservice-bridge's outcomeFrom implementation, which is not present in the tree.
The exact default of ircClient.getMaxLineLength() (matrix-org-irc) is not in the tree; the negative-length condition depends on it plus the length of the homeserver-supplied media URI.

Whether the hidden fix for the reply route uses getIntent(event.sender) (CWE-280) or checks eventContent.room_id against event.room_id was not verifiable offline; both are consistent with the missing protection recorded in T1.
